suggestions.issue: Internal self-contradiction that would mislead a student. The definition and plain_english state bottom-up 'starts at the source (mic/input) and works forward toward the output,' but purpose_function and practical_application state it starts at 'the lowest level / physical/electrical layer / output' and works UP toward the source (e.g. 'confirm the amplifier and speakers work first, then move back through processing, console, and source'). These are opposite directions. Web-verified via howtonetwork.com and Cisco Press (ciscopress.com) troubleshooting-methodology references: bottom-up begins at the bottom/physical layer (cables, connectors, output/foundation end) and works UP toward the application/source — matching this entry's purpose_function and practical_application. So the definition and plain_english are the incorrect/contradictory fields.
suggestions.suggestion: Rewrite definition and plain_english to match the standard (and the entry's own purpose_function/practical_application): bottom-up troubleshooting starts at the output/lowest (physical/electrical) end of the chain — e.g. amp and speakers — and works back toward the source, verifying each foundational stage before higher-level causes. Remove the 'starting at the source and working toward the output' wording, which describes the opposite (top-down/source-first) direction.
